binaries.name: memprocfs
binaries.why: Mount a memory image as a file system: processes, handles, modules, registry and network state become files. The mem_fs tool starts it for one call, lists or exports chosen files into the job's output and stops it. AGPL-3.0, so its licence and this project's combine where Volatility's do not. libfuse2 is the library only: a usable mount also needs a /dev/fuse the worker may open and a fusermount3 or fusermount helper, and whether a worker has them is a fact of the image and the harness; mem_fs reports which of them the host has when a mount fails.

binaries.name: vol
binaries.why: The plugin framework most reports cite. Kept at an executable boundary rather than imported or vendored, under its own Volatility Software License 1.0.

data.name: vol-windows-symbols
data.why: Windows kernel symbol tables for `vol`, so a Windows plugin finds its kernel's symbols with no network (run it with `--offline`). The Volatility Foundation's `windows.zip`, a bundle of 2019 (last changed 2019-10-16): tables for the Windows builds of that time, not every one of them. A newer kernel is not in it; `vol -q isfinfo` lists the tables there are.
data.licence: Our reading, not legal advice. The pack carries no licence text of its own. The Volatility Software License 1.0 (https://www.volatilityfoundation.org/license/vsl-v1.0) says its "Software" includes "any data (such as operating system profiles or configuration information)" provided with the software; we read the tables as such data. The tables are generated from Microsoft's public symbol (PDB) files, whose Microsoft Symbol Server licence terms of June 2022 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/legal/windows-sdk/microsoft-symbol-server-license-terms) allow use "solely for purposes of performance, security or functional debugging and testing of your software as used with Microsoft software, or as otherwise authorized by Microsoft" and say that you may not "share, publish, rent, or lease the Symbol Items, or provide the Symbol Items as stand-alone offerings for others to use". Microsoft's terms grant use for debugging and testing your software; whether examining a third party's memory image falls inside that is not decided here, so these terms may bear on use as well as on redistribution. This image is not for redistribution.

binaries.name: avml
binaries.why: Acquire memory from a live Linux host into a portable format, without building a kernel module. It is declared so the operator has the pinned binary and checksum to take to the source host; run in an analysis VM it captures that VM, not the subject.

binaries.name: strings
binaries.why: A first pass over a region before a parser is chosen. Always search UTF-16LE as well, which strings -el does.

binaries.name: yara
binaries.why: Scan a whole memory image or a dumped process region with examiner-supplied rules, preserving rule names, matching strings and byte offsets (match bytes can be secret: run the job with secret_output: true). This is the standalone scanner: Volatility's YARA plugins need a Python binding that no requirement of this pack installs.

binaries.name: aeskeyfind
binaries.why: Find AES-128 and AES-256 key schedules in a memory image by testing each position against the key-expansion constraints; it tolerates a few decayed bits. A candidate is a lead, and is established only by decrypting something the evidence holds with it. Debian packages it for amd64 and i386 only: this one is built from Debian's source and patches (files over 4 GB among them) on every architecture.

install.apt: built from source 1.0-11 (install.build): Debian packages it for amd64 and i386 only

binaries.name: gcc
binaries.why: Compile a small C program the seat itself writes, in the job's own directory: a scanner over a memory image too large for Python to hold, a decoder for a format no library reads. The source and the build line stay in the record like any other tool. Never a program or a source tree the evidence holds: nothing from the evidence is executed.

binaries.name: make
binaries.why: Build a tool distributed as source, from a tree the operator or a pack supplied; never a source tree the evidence holds.
